transcription.source: LAC microfilm images, LAC e000874955-e000874967 (13 images)
transcription.notes: Transcribed 5 Nov 2026 from enlarged half-spread crops; no group is cut at the gutter. Reader pass 5 Nov 2026 against all 13 images: 21 groups corrected (the hand's 5 read as 3 or the reverse: 301->501 in six places, 329->529, 341->541, 382->582, 303->305, 303->503, 381->581, 633->635, 533->535, 533->553, 255->235, 30->50); the written ordinals 1o-4o are figures, not cipher groups (bracketed).

system.summary: 700-entry table of numbered words, place and ship names, syllables and single letters (1757 Vaudreuil table), with names and titles left in clear and phonetic spelling.
system.sibling_key: Key found for catalogue 1391 (vaudreuil1760): the 1757 Vaudreuil table ANOM COL C11E 10 f.289 (LAC e001295274); it fits this letter from the first line.
system.notes: Table in numerical order only on the sheet used (the alphabetical sheets e001295267/69 give the same entries by word).

conditions.human_role: Asked for the sibling letters of catalogue 1391 to be decoded and then made into targets of their own.

solution.what: Table found for catalogue 1391 (same hand, same office, months apart) tried on this letter: function words fall in place.
Images fetched from the LAC image server with curl -L (about half the requests need a retry).

Decoded with the table and its context-corrected cells (key/overrides.json); 12 groups sit on a cell still doubtful and 0 are cut at the gutter; the decode reads as French throughout but no reader has reviewed it as sentences.

Written ordinals 1o-4o (f.54-) are figures, not cipher groups: bracketed in transcription.txt and removed from ct.txt (the decode had read them as cell 1 etc.). Overrides synchronised with cat. 1391 (cell 2 = campagne).

Reader review: fetched the 13 images, compared every half-page with the transcription and the decode, corrected 21 groups (5/3 slips, 301 trou -> 501 ois in six places) and decoded the letter as sentences; wrote reading.md, reading_en.md, reading_notes.md. The same slip (301->501) was found in cat. 1389.

Cells settled from the letter: 656 = q (cinq, cinquante, conséquent), 505 = am, 9 = possession, 289 = os; overrides copied to cat. 1389, 1390 and 1391. 23 groups stay unread (the Sulpicians' groups on f.64r, 'ap se e ment' on f.60v and 9 others).

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The 1757 Vaudreuil table (ANOM COL C11E 10, LAC e001295274), found to fit catalogue 1391 of the same hand, applied to this letter.

texts.label: ANOM, COL C11A 104, ff.54-66 (CABAC_PIAF_60891)
texts.summary: Vaudreuil reports to the minister on the winter and the defence plan: famine and loss of draught animals, a British army of about 20-25 000 against Niagara, Fort Duquesne evacuated, the four points to defend (Carillon, the Belle Rivière, Niagara, La Présentation and Lake Ontario), his plan to fall back on Québec with his troops, and numbered requests for battalions, munitions and provisions.

reading_review.by: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (a model reading, not a person), after the solving passes
reading_review.note: Read the French sentence by sentence against reading_en.md and the images: the whole letter builds coherent 1759 chancery French (the census of the three governments, the four points to defend, the plan to meet the English at Québec, the request for troops, munitions and a supplement of provisions). 21 groups corrected on the images, 23 unread, one cell (403) odd, one syllable group (s-in-d-re = moindre) read twice by sense. Not checked by a person.

outcome.notes: Read as sentences against the images on 5 Nov 2026 (model reading, no outside reader). Key found, not recovered; table cells read from the images of the volume. Four more cells settled from this letter (656 q, 505 am, 9 possession, 289 os).
